title: Use watchman for centralized filesystem watching instead of direct inotify
description:
Replace the 5-second polling discovery loop with watchman event subscriptions for real-time instance detection.

Currently discovery polls $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/rqbit/ every 5 seconds for new/departed .sock files. This adds up to 5s latency before a new instance is detected and routing table convergence begins.

Watchman advantages over direct inotify:
- Centralized: one watchman daemon serves all processes watching the same directory, instead of each rqbit instance creating its own inotify watcher (kernel inotify watch limits are a real constraint)
- Cross-platform: works on macOS (FSEvents), Linux (inotify), Windows (ReadDirectoryChangesW) via a single API
- Robust: handles edge cases (rename, move, cookie grouping, overflow recovery) that raw inotify requires manual handling for
- Subscription model: persistent Unix socket connection, events pushed as they happen
- Deduped: if N rqbit instances all watch the same dir, watchman maintains one kernel watch

Implementation:
1. Add watchman client dependency (watchman_client crate or raw Unix socket protocol via watchmanctl JSON)
2. On coordinator start: connect to watchman daemon, subscribe to $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/rqbit/ with expression matching *.sock files
3. Replace spawn_discovery_loop's poll interval with watchman event stream reader
4. On create event: connect_to_peer for new instance
5. On delete event: remove_peer for departed instance
6. Graceful fallback: if watchman daemon is not running, fall back to polling (existing implementation)

The fallback to polling is important — watchman may not be installed on all systems. The coordinator should detect watchman availability at startup and select the appropriate discovery backend.

This ticket supersedes the inotify portion of rqbit-reuseport-discovery. If watchman is available, use it; otherwise the existing poll loop remains.

title: sslh-style auto-detection of postcard vs varlink on incoming connections
description:
Auto-detect the wire format of incoming IPC connections by peeking at the first byte, like sslh protocol multiplexing. This lets mixed-format instances interoperate without configuration.

Detection heuristic:
- Varlink messages are JSON objects starting with '{' (0x7B), terminated by NUL
- Postcard frames start with a binary length prefix (u32 BE) followed by compact binary data
- Peek first byte via recv(MSG_PEEK) on the Unix socket:
  - 0x7B ('{') -> varlink JSON
  - 0x01-0x04 (small variant tags / mode bytes) -> postcard
  - If ambiguous, try postcard first, fall back to varlink on parse error

Flow:
1. Accept Unix socket connection
2. MSG_PEEK first byte
3. Select decoder (postcard or varlink reader)
4. Proceed with normal connection handling

This makes the format negotiation automatic and transparent. New instances could use varlink by default while still accepting connections from older postcard-only instances.

Depends on both rqbit-reuseport-postcard and rqbit-reuseport-varlink being implemented.

Acceptance criteria:
- Instance using varlink can accept connection from instance using postcard (and vice versa)
- Detection is zero-copy (MSG_PEEK, no consumed byte)
- .design/reuseport-multi-instance.md updated with auto-detection section
- Fallback behavior documented for ambiguous first bytes

title: Add varlink IDL interface and make it the default RPC protocol
description:
Define the inter-instance coordination interface as a varlink IDL, generate Rust types, and make varlink the default wire format. Replaces postcard as the default (postcard remains as a cfg feature for constrained environments).

Scope:
1. Write a .varlink IDL file (e.g. crates/librqbit/src/instances/org.rqbit.Instance.varlink) defining:
   - Hello(instance_id: string) -> ()
   - TorrentsAdded(info_hashes: [][]byte) -> ()
   - TorrentsRemoved(info_hashes: [][]byte) -> ()
   - WhoHas(info_hash: []byte) -> IHas(info_hash: []byte) | error
   - Goodbye() -> ()
   - ForwardTcp(peer_addr: string, handshake: []byte, extra: []byte) -> stream
2. Use varlink crate codegen (build.rs or varlink_rust_generator) to generate Rust client/server types
3. Messages are JSON on the wire, each terminated by NUL byte (varlink standard framing)
4. varlink error handling for unsupported methods, not found, etc.
5. Make varlink the default (no feature flag needed); postcard behind --features postcard-rpc
6. ForwardTcp as a varlink streaming call (varlink supports streamed responses)

Varlink advantages:
- Human-readable wire format (JSON) — easy debugging with socat/nc
- Language-agnostic IDL — other implementations (Go, Python, C) can use the interface
- Standard error model
- Mature Rust codegen

Depends on rqbit-reuseport-postcard (build the typed message structures first, then port to varlink).

Acceptance criteria:
- cargo check (default features) uses varlink
- cargo check --features postcard-rpc uses postcard
- .varlink IDL committed
- .design/reuseport-multi-instance.md updated: varlink is documented as default, postcard as alternative
- Both formats can talk to same InstanceCoordinator logic (format is a wire concern, not logic)

title: Replace hand-rolled wire protocol with serde + postcard serialization
description:
Replace the manual binary encode/decode functions in instances/protocol.rs with serde-derived message types serialized via postcard.

Scope:
1. Add postcard crate dependency (cfg feature 'postcard-rpc', not default)
2. Define typed message enums with #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]:
   - ControlMessage: Hello { instance_id }, TorrentsAdded { info_hashes }, TorrentsRemoved { info_hashes }, WhoHas { info_hash }, IHas { info_hash }, Goodbye
   - InstanceMessage: Control(ControlMessage), ForwardTcp(ForwardTcpMetadata { peer_addr, handshake, extra })
3. Replace protocol.rs encode/decode functions with postcard::to_allocvec / from_bytes
4. Framing: [u32 BE: len][postcard bytes] — postcard output is not self-delimiting
5. Mode byte stays for connection multiplexing (control vs forward), or fold into InstanceMessage enum variant
6. SocketAddr serialization via serde (postcard handles it natively)
7. Keep the existing protocol.rs as fallback when feature is disabled (or replace entirely)

Advantages over hand-rolled:
- Type-safe serialization, no manual offset arithmetic
- Id20 ([u8;20]) serializes natively
- SocketAddr serializes natively (no manual family byte)
- Adding new message types is just adding an enum variant
- Postcard is compact (varint encoding), comparable to manual binary

Not the default initially — feature flag only. varlink becomes the default in rqbit-reuseport-varlink.

Acceptance criteria:
- cargo check with --features postcard-rpc passes
- Existing tests pass
- .design/reuseport-multi-instance.md updated with postcard protocol section
- Wire format documented with example bytes
notes: Implemented: serde-derived ControlMessage and ForwardTcpMeta types in protocol.rs. Cfg-gated encode/decode: postcard::to_allocvec/from_bytes with --features postcard-rpc, manual binary encoding by default. Coordinator updated to use typed ControlMessage enum throughout (handle_control_message, broadcast, send_to_peer, announce/unannounce). ForwardTcpMeta replaces manual metadata encoding. Both configs: clippy clean, 31 tests pass. Design doc updated with dual-format wire protocol section. Commit: forthcoming

title: IGD port forwarding sharing across instances
description:
Make UPnP/IGD port forwarding work when multiple instances share the same listen port. This is the original goal that motivated the entire reuseport effort.

Changes to crates/upnp:
1. Tolerate 718 ConflictInMappingEntry on AddPortMapping SOAP call — another instance already created the mapping for this port. Treat as success (forward_port in crates/upnp/src/lib.rs:80-136).
2. Coordinate lease renewal: with N instances all renewing, either:
   a. First-come wins (all try, failures are ignored since the mapping exists)
   b. Elect a renewal leader via the IPC protocol (one instance renews, others just verify)
3. On instance shutdown: do NOT delete the port mapping if other instances are still running. Check via IPC if any peer instance still needs the port before calling DeletePortMapping.

The simplest initial approach: just tolerate 718 on add, let all instances renew independently (idempotent), skip DeletePortMapping if peer instances exist.
notes:
Implemented: forward_port() now parses SOAP fault responses. Error 718 (ConflictInMappingEntry) is tolerated as success — another instance already has the mapping. Other SOAP errors include errorCode + errorDescription in the bail message for observability.

No other changes needed:
- manage_port() infinite loop (every lease_duration/2 = 30s) IS the renewal/deadline scheduler. If mapping disappears, next tick re-creates it.
- No DeletePortMapping call exists — mappings expire naturally when leases lapse. Correct for multi-instance: one instance shutting down doesn't kill shared mapping.
- All instances independently call AddPortMapping. First succeeds, rest get 718 (tolerated). All independently renew.

Also: download handler no longer force-disables UPnP when --reuseport is set, so shared port forwarding works.

Commit: forthcoming

title: Extend --reuseport to server, share, and desktop commands
description:
Once the core multi-instance infrastructure is proven on the download command, extend --reuseport to:
- rqbit server (long-running, many torrents, HTTP API)
- rqbit share
- desktop (Tauri app)

Considerations:
- server mode may want different defaults (always-on reuseport?)
- desktop needs the XDG runtime dir socket to coexist with potential multiple desktop instances
- Document multi-instance setup in README/man pages

title: uTP multi-instance reuseport design (long-term)
description:
Design and eventually implement uTP support for multi-instance port sharing. Currently blocked by librqbit-utp-0.7.0 hardcoding reuseport:false internally (socket.rs:751).

Required librqbit-utp changes (fork or upstream):
1. Add reuseport:bool to SocketOpts or UtpSocketUdpOpts (trivial change)
2. Add raw datagram hook: callback or channel exposing every incoming datagram before the uTP stack processes it
3. Add inject_datagram(addr, bytes) API: inject a forwarded datagram into the uTP state machine

Two approaches documented:

Approach A - Raw datagram forwarding over IPC:
- Instance B receives uTP datagram, checks conn_id, doesn't own it
- Forwards [src_addr, datagram_bytes] to owning instance via ForwardUtpDatagram IPC mode
- Owning instance injects into its uTP stack
- Pro: preserves original source address
- Con: every misrouted datagram crosses IPC, latency overhead

Approach B - Dedicated socket + fd handoff with uTP state migration:
- Instance B receives uTP SYN, creates new UDP socket on ephemeral port
- Passes fd + uTP initial state (conn_id, seq_nr, ack_nr) to owning instance via SCM_RIGHTS
- Owning instance sends SYN-ACK from new socket; peer migrates (uTP handles NAT rebinding)
- Pro: after handoff, zero overhead
- Con: complex, needs uTP state extract/inject API

Initial scope: DESIGN ONLY. Pick approach, document tradeoffs, prototype librqbit-utp changes.

title: Session hooks: announce/unannounce torrents to peer instances
description:
Hook into Session::add_torrent_internal (session.rs:1218-1408) and Session::delete (session.rs:1423-1509) to broadcast torrent ownership changes to peer instances.

On torrent add (after DB insert at line 1386): coordinator.announce_torrent(info_hash) -> sends TorrentsAdded to all connected instances.
On torrent delete (after DB remove at line 1440): coordinator.unannounce_torrent(info_hash) -> sends TorrentsRemoved.
On new instance discovered (Hello exchange): send full current torrent set (all info_hashes from session DB).

Also handle AlreadyManaged case (session.rs:1335): if already managed, the torrent was already announced, so skip re-announcing unless this is a different instance (shouldn't happen within one process).

The coordinator reference lives on Session (Option<Arc<InstanceCoordinator>>) or is passed via ListenerOptions/SessionOptions.
notes: Implemented: announce_torrent called after managed_torrent.start() in add_torrent_internal. unannounce_torrent called after db.remove in delete. SessionForwardHandler implements ForwardHandler trait, routes forwarded connections through check_incoming_connection with allow_forward=false. Commit: 734b5136

title: Listener integration: handshake peek + routing decision
description:
Integrate the multi-instance routing into the TCP accept loop (session.rs task_listener, lines 970-1013).

After accepting a TCP connection and before handing it to check_incoming_connection:
1. Read the first 68 bytes (BT handshake) using ReadBuf::read_handshake
2. Extract info_hash from Handshake struct
3. Check local torrents (existing linear scan in check_incoming_connection, session.rs:943-950)
4. If found locally -> handle normally (existing path)
5. If not found AND coordinator is active -> lookup routing table
   a. If found -> fd handoff to owning instance (rqbit-reuseport-fd-handoff)
   b. If not found -> drop connection (or WhoHas broadcast, optional)
6. If reuseport is NOT active -> existing behavior (no routing)

Key constraint: the 68-byte handshake must be passed along in both paths. For local handling: inject into ReadBuf (existing read_buf already does this). For fd handoff: send as metadata alongside the fd.
notes: Implemented: check_incoming_connection in session.rs now takes allow_forward:bool. On local torrent miss, looks up routing table and calls coordinator.forward_tcp_stream(). Forwarded connections use allow_forward=false to prevent loops. ReadBuf::drain_remaining() added to extract pre-read bytes. Commit: 734b5136

title: TCP fd handoff via SCM_RIGHTS (zero-copy)
description:
When an instance receives a TCP connection for a torrent it does not own, hand off the raw TCP fd to the owning instance via SCM_RIGHTS ancillary data over the Unix IPC socket.

Flow:
1. Accept TCP, read 68-byte BT handshake, extract info_hash
2. Lookup routing table -> owning instance_id
3. Connect to owning instance Unix socket in ForwardTcpFd mode
4. Send metadata: peer_addr + handshake bytes (pre-read, need to be replayed)
5. Send TCP fd via SCM_RIGHTS (sendmsg with ancillary data)
6. Receiver: fd -> tokio TcpStream via from_std(from_raw_fd(fd)), inject handshake bytes into ReadBuf, handle natively

Zero data-copy: the receiving instance reads/writes directly to the peer. No proxy pipe through the forwarding instance.

Dependencies: nix or libc crate for sendmsg/recvmsg with SCM_RIGHTS. tokio AsyncFd or from_std for wrapping the received fd.
notes: DEFERRED in favor of stream proxy: Instead of SCM_RIGHTS fd passing, we implemented a stream proxy approach — the forwarder connects to the target instance Unix socket, writes forward metadata (peer_addr + handshake bytes + extra bytes), then does bidirectional pipe via tokio::io::copy. This works with the existing BoxAsyncReadVectored/BoxAsyncWrite trait objects without needing raw fd access. PrefixedReader replays consumed handshake bytes on the receive side. SCM_RIGHTS remains a future zero-copy optimization.

title: Instance discovery via XDG runtime dir (inotify + poll)
description:
Instance discovery by watching $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/rqbit/ for socket files.

Optional inotify watcher (Linux only, behind a feature flag or cfg): real-time IN_CREATE/IN_DELETE events on the directory for socket file appearance/disappearance. Triggers immediate connect to new instances and cleanup of departed ones.

Polling fallback: scan directory every N seconds (default 5s) for non-Linux platforms or when inotify init fails.

On new socket discovered: connect control connection, exchange Hello + full torrent list. On socket disappeared: remove instance from routing table, close control connection.

Socket naming: <pid>-<short-random>.sock to avoid collisions. Stale socket detection (connect fails) → cleanup.
notes:
PARTIALLY DONE: Polling-based discovery implemented (5s interval scan of socket dir). inotify watcher NOT yet implemented. Stale socket cleanup uses synchronous connect-test. Commit: 734b5136
IMPLEMENTED: Replaced 5s poll with notify-based real-time discovery. notify made non-optional (removed 'watch' feature gate, made pub mod watch always available). spawn_discovery_loop now creates a notify::RecommendedWatcher on socket_dir, filters events to *.sock paths, calls discover_peers() on each event. Poll backstop retained at 60s interval (was 5s) for missed-event recovery. Watcher init failure falls back to poll-only automatically. Commits follow.

title: Materialized routing table (info_hash to instance map)
description:
Thread-safe routing table mapping Id20 (info_hash) to Set<instance_id>. Maintained proactively via control protocol announcements (TorrentsAdded/Removed on torrent add/delete). Read-accessible from the listener accept loop with minimal contention (RwLock or lock-free read).

On new instance connection (Hello exchange): request full torrent list. On WhoHas query: respond with IHas if we own the info_hash. Supports the lookup(info_hash) -> Option<instance_id> API used by the fd-handoff path.

Edge case: multiple instances have the same torrent (e.g., same torrent added to two instances) — return any, or round-robin for load balancing.
notes: Implemented: RoutingTable in routing.rs with parking_lot::RwLock<HashMap<[u8;20], HashSet<InstanceId>>>. Supports add/add_many/remove/remove_instance/lookup. Commit: 734b5136

title: IPC wire protocol for inter-instance communication
description:
Binary length-prefixed wire protocol over Unix domain sockets. First byte of each connection selects mode:

0x01 Control (persistent): Hello { instance_id, announce_port }, TorrentsAdded { info_hashes: Vec<Id20> }, TorrentsRemoved { info_hashes }, WhoHas { info_hash }, IHas { info_hash }, Goodbye
0x02 ForwardTcpFd (one-shot): metadata frame { peer_addr: SocketAddr, handshake_bytes: Vec<u8> } + TCP fd passed via SCM_RIGHTS ancillary data. Receiver takes ownership of fd.
0x03 ForwardUtpDatagram (future): { src_addr, datagram_bytes } for raw uTP datagram forwarding.

Framing: [u32 BE length][u8 msg_type][payload]. Id20 = 20 bytes raw.
notes: Implemented: Binary length-prefixed wire protocol in protocol.rs. Control mode (0x01): Hello, TorrentsAdded/Removed, WhoHas/IHas, Goodbye. Forward mode (0x02): metadata frame with SocketAddr + handshake + extra bytes, then bidirectional pipe. Commit: 734b5136

title: Instance coordinator module
description: New module (or crate) managing the instance identity and lifecycle in the multi-instance coordination system. Creates a Unix domain socket at $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/rqbit/<instance-id>.sock. Owns the control protocol state, routing table, and discovery loop. Provides the high-level API that listener and session integration use: announce_torrent, unannounce_torrent, lookup(info_hash) -> Option<instance_id>, forward_tcp_fd(instance_id, fd, peer_addr, handshake_bytes).
notes: Implemented: InstanceCoordinator in crates/librqbit/src/instances/coordinator.rs. Manages XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/rqbit/<id>.sock, discovery loop (poll-based), control connections, forward listener, routing table. Commit: 734b5136

title: CLI --reuseport flag on download command
description: Add --reuseport (env: RQBIT_REUSEPORT) flag to the download subcommand only. When set: threads reuseport:bool through ListenerOptions to BindOpts for the TCP listener (currently hardcoded false in listen.rs:105), activates the instance coordinator, enables handshake peek + routing in accept loop. Do NOT add to server/share/desktop yet — rqbit-reuseport-broader covers that.
notes: Implemented: --reuseport flag added to DownloadOpts with RQBIT_REUSEPORT env var. Threads reuseport:bool through ListenerOptions to TCP BindOpts. Commit: 734b5136

title: Multi-instance SO_REUSEPORT peer connection sharing
description:
Run multiple `rqbit download` instances on the same host sharing the same TCP listen port via SO_REUSEPORT. Incoming peer connections are routed to the correct instance based on the BT handshake info_hash, using an IPC protocol over Unix domain sockets in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR.

Each instance announces its torrent set; a materialized routing table enables targeted connection forwarding. TCP connections are handed off zero-copy via SCM_RIGHTS fd passing.

Architecture:
- XDG runtime dir sockets: $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/rqbit/<instance-id>.sock
- Control protocol: Hello, TorrentsAdded/Removed, WhoHas/IHas, Goodbye
- Forward protocol: ForwardTcpFd (metadata + fd via SCM_RIGHTS)
- Discovery: inotify (optional) + directory poll fallback
- Routing key: info_hash from BT handshake (first 68 bytes)

This enables the end goal: multiple instances sharing a single IGD port forwarding rule on the router.
